result:
Scratch file is confirmed removed. Summary of the fix (per ADR 0003, which supersedes the outdated product notes):

1. **Reserved/short/non-Latin names** (`src/lib/slug.ts`, `src/server/services/organization-service.ts`): `uniqueSlug()` now treats a too-short base the same as a reserved one, falling through to the numeric-suffix loop instead of returning an invalid slug. `createOrganization()` now validates the slug *after* deriving/deduplicating it instead of before, so derivation gets the chance to fix up a reserved or too-short candidate instead of being refused outright.

2. **Case-insensitive email** (`src/server/repositories/user-repository.ts`): `findUserByEmail` and `insertUser` now lowercase the address themselves rather than trusting every caller to have already done so, so storage and lookup always agree regardless of entry point.

3. **No throttle on sign-up / wrong error on throttled sign-in** (`src/actions/auth/register.ts`, `src/lib/errors.ts`): sign-up now consumes the `auth:register` rate-limit bucket before doing anything, mirroring login/reset-password. Separately, `toAppError()` previously only recognized a hardcoded list of service-layer error classes — every action-layer error (`RateLimitedError`, `PlanLimitError`, etc.) fell through to a generic `internal_error`. It now also honors any thrown error's own declared `code` field generically, so throttling (and other action errors) map to their real `ErrorCode`/HTTP status everywhere instead of "Something went wrong."

4. **Inconsistent duplicate-address handling** (`src/lib/auth-errors.ts`, `src/server/services/auth-service.ts`): sign-up against an existing address now throws a dedicated `EmailAlreadyExistsError` (code `conflict`) instead of a generic `Error`, so it's refused consistently as the ADR specifies.

5. **Oversized workspace name** (`src/schemas/organization.ts`, `src/server/services/auth-service.ts`): added a shared `ORG_NAME_MAX_LENGTH` constant, and sign-up now shortens the display name so `"<name>'s workspace"` always fits the limit the org schema enforces, so the settings form never inherits an unsavable name.

Verified with the full existing test suite (617 tests, all passing), typecheck, lint, and a temporary scratch test (since removed) covering all five scenarios directly against the service/action layer.
